items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...maybe a little of the Neville Brothers. ... [INTERVIEWEE] Right.

ctx.x: He was a true artist man. I think he was really a true artist. Not only with music but fashion and visual art. Yeah he was what I call a true artist. And a lot of people didn’t like what he was doing toward the end but I loved it and I love it man, I love Miles.

You know I think the average person when they think of New Orleans music they probably typecast it into well yes, I know Dixieland jazz came from there and maybe a little of the Neville Brothers. I don’t know, I count myself in this category, that I didn’t realize how much — different kinds of things were actually coming out of New Orleans.

Right. And even now as we try to rebuild and regroup, there’s been a part of New Orleans music and New Orleans culture for instance that has not been embraced and mainly it’s the really avante garde sorry to say. I don’t like the word but that’s the type of musician Kidd Jordan is. The kind of musician I am too because I can do that as well as play, because it’s all the same thing. But unless you sound something like Louis Armstrong or whatever like that man, it’s like it doesn’t matter. Whatever you do it…
